headline: High: B can ingest A’s content and send it to third-party APIs, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risk in the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a content-writing agent with broad network egress; B is a document-processing agent that uses browsers and MCP and accepts natural-language commands. The pair has a plausible content-to-instructions bridge, but no shared filesystem or direct ingestion path is documented, so I rate this medium rather than high.
conditions: IF A’s generated text is pasted into B as instructions or source material
IF B parses A-authored content from files or browser output as trusted commands
mitigations: Require a human review step before B executes any A-authored text
Prefix A outputs as untrusted content in the workflow
Disable automatic tool execution on parsed document text
Use a separate workspace for A and B
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all A outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly touches PDFs, text, images, diagrams, and API keys, and can call multiple third-party model APIs; A has broad network egress. If A supplies sensitive content to B, B can transmit it outward by default, so the leakage blast radius is high.
conditions: IF A provides sensitive documents or secrets to B
IF B routes those inputs to any listed external API
mitigations: Restrict B to local-only models
Block API-keyed providers in B
Remove secrets from inputs before processing
Use a redaction pass on A outputs before B sees them
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists per document class

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has broad network egress and B has broad network egress plus browser/MCP access and multiple-instance support. They do not show shared write surfaces, but they do overlap on mutable networked actions, so conflict is plausible in default use and not merely theoretical.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same remote service or API quota
IF A and B are run concurrently against the same mutable network resource
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials to A and B
Serialize access to shared remote resources
Limit B browser sessions to read-only sites
Set per-agent rate limits
requires-engineering: add distributed locking for shared network targets

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a content-writing agent, so its outputs are likely to be consumed by B’s document-processing pipeline. B’s natural-language tool-use pattern and multi-API access mean unverified A output can cascade into downstream actions, but there is no direct evidence of autonomous irreversible action-taking.
conditions: IF B treats A’s generated text as authoritative input
IF B forwards A-derived claims into browser or API actions without verification
mitigations: Add a verification step before B acts on A output
Require citations for any A-derived factual claim
Constrain B to draft-only mode
Log A-to-B handoffs for review
requires-engineering: implement claim-checking before tool calls

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles API keys and multiple external AI providers, while A has broad network egress. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so I cannot prove a breach, but the documented external processing and secret handling create a plausible compliance mismatch that is more than low risk.
conditions: IF regulated or residency-bound data is sent through B
IF A forwards that data to external services via network egress
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B
Disable non-approved external providers in B
Use region-locked endpoints only
Review retention settings for each provider
requires-engineering: map data classes to approved processing regions
